name: India
note: Deaths are reported to the local Registrar within 21 days: by the head of household for home deaths, and by the hospital or other institution for deaths there. Hospitals must also certify the cause of death, and cremation and burial ground keepers report each death as well. Since the 2023 amendment, every registration feeds a State unified database on the Registrar General's portal and a national database. That database may, on request, update the population register, electoral rolls, Aadhaar, ration cards, passports, driving licences and property registration. Anyone may obtain a death certificate without the cause of death, but there is no official route for banks or insurers to check deaths.

steps.title: Medical institution certifies the cause of death to the Registrar
steps.localName: Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD)
steps.who: Every medical institution (public or private), signed by the attending medical practitioner.
steps.summary: Since the 2023 amendment every medical institution must, free of charge, send the Registrar a certificate of the cause of death (MCCD, Form 4) and give a copy to the nearest relative; refusal is an offence.

steps.title: Attending doctor certifies cause of death for deaths outside institutions
steps.who: The medical practitioner who attended the deceased during the recent illness.
steps.summary: The attending practitioner must issue the cause-of-death certificate (Form 4A) to the informant, who hands it to the Registrar when reporting the death.

steps.title: Medical or health attendant notifies the death
steps.who: Medical or health attendants present at the death, and other persons the State designates.
steps.summary: Separately from the informant, a medical or health attendant present at a death must notify it to the Registrar in the prescribed manner. No statutory rule on who may pronounce death was found.

steps.title: Officer conducting an inquest reports the death
steps.trigger: A death in which an inquest is held.
steps.summary: Where an inquest is held, the inquest officer gives the registration information; deserted bodies are reported by the village headman or the local police station officer.

steps.title: Head of household reports the death to the Registrar
steps.who: For deaths at home: the head of the house/household, else the nearest relative present, else the oldest adult present.

deadline.text: within 21 days (Model Rules; each State prescribes)

steps.summary: Information may be given orally or in writing and is entered in the reporting form (Form 2) with the informant's signature. Late registration is possible with a fee (to 30 days), District Registrar permission (to 1 year) or a magistrate's order. Failure to report is punishable by a fine of up to ₹250.

steps.title: Institution reports deaths that occur in it
steps.who: The medical officer in charge of a hospital, health centre, nursing home etc.; jailors; persons in charge of hostels, lodging houses and similar places.

deadline.text: within 21 days (Model Rules; each State prescribes)

steps.summary: For institutional deaths the institution itself is the informant, with a fine of up to ₹1,000 per death for failing to report. States register on the portal approved by the Registrar General (the CRS portal).

steps.title: Cremation or burial ground keeper notifies the death
steps.who: The keeper or owner of a place for disposal of dead bodies, or the person the local authority requires to be present there.
steps.summary: Burial and cremation grounds are a second reporting channel: the keeper must notify each death to the Registrar. The Act does not make disposal conditional on a registration certificate.

steps.title: Registrar gives the informant a death certificate
steps.who: The local Registrar (municipal or panchayat registrar).

deadline.text: not later than seven days after registration

steps.summary: The Registrar must issue an extract certificate free of charge, electronically or otherwise, within seven days of registration; failing to do so is an offence.

steps.title: Any person may search the register and obtain a death certificate
steps.who: Any person, on payment of fees under State rules.
steps.summary: Any person may have the register searched and obtain a certified death certificate, which is evidence of the death, but the cause of death is never shown on a certificate.

steps.title: Registrar's data goes into the State unified database
steps.who: Registrars, to the Chief Registrar of the State, on the RGI-approved portal.
steps.summary: Since the 2023 amendment every Registrar must share registration data with a unified State database kept by the Chief Registrar, which may on request be made available to other State databases.

steps.title: State data shared with the national database of the Registrar General of India
steps.who: Chief Registrars and Registrars, to the Registrar General of India.
steps.summary: The Registrar General of India keeps a national database of registered births and deaths, and Chief Registrars and Registrars must share their data with it. (Within the actor list this is recorded as the population-register hop; the National Population Register itself is a separate database fed on request.)

steps.title: National database made available to population register, electoral rolls, Aadhaar, ration cards, passports, driving licences and property registration
steps.who: Authorities maintaining the National Population Register, electoral rolls, Aadhaar, ration cards, passports, driving licences, property registration and other notified national databases.
steps.trigger: Request by the authority, with Central Government approval.
steps.summary: The 2023 amendment allows the national database to be made available, on request and with Central Government approval, to the bodies keeping these databases, which must report back the action taken. Data flows are permitted rather than mandated per death.

steps.title: Electoral roll authorities may draw on the death database
steps.who: The authorities preparing electoral rolls (subject to the Representation of the People Act, 1950).
steps.summary: Electoral rolls are expressly listed among the databases the national death database may feed, without prejudice to the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

steps.title: Returns and cause-of-death certificates to the Chief Registrar for statistics
steps.who: Registrars, to the Chief Registrar; MCCD certificates by the 10th of the following month.

deadline.text: MCCD forms by the 10th of the following month

steps.summary: Registrars send periodic returns and the medical cause-of-death certificates to the Chief Registrar, who publishes an annual statistical report.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: 21 days under the Model Rules 1999, which each State adopts; the Act leaves the time to be prescribed.

informantDuty.note: Head of household for home deaths; the medical officer in charge for institutional deaths; jailors and others for their premises; village headman/police for deserted bodies.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent scrutiny of MCCDs; inquests are held by police/magistrates under criminal procedure.

electronicRegistration.note: States must register on the RGI-approved portal and certificates may be issued electronically, but household informants may still report orally or on paper.

centralPopulationRegister.name: National database of registered births and deaths (Registrar General of India); National Population Register is separate
centralPopulationRegister.note: The RBD national database is not itself a population register; the NPR may draw on it on request.

governmentPropagation.note: Registration flows automatically to the State and national databases; onward use by the population register, electoral rolls, Aadhaar, ration cards, passports, driving licences and property registration is on request with Central Government approval.

certificateAccess.note: Any person may obtain a death certificate; cause of death is never disclosed on it.

privateSectorVerification.note: The Act provides no route for banks or insurers to check the database; they rely on certificates, which anyone may obtain.

gaps: crsorgi.gov.in (CRS portal), censusindia.gov.in, egazette.gov.in and the apex indiacode.nic.in were refused or unreachable; the CRS portal citation is the host only. Text was read through indiacode.gov.in's DSpace API.
The 2023 Amendment Act's commencement date (reported as 1 October 2023) was not confirmed from the Gazette notification; the India Code consolidated sections already show the amendments.
The 21-day deadline comes from the Model Rules 1999; individual State rules (e.g. Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh) were not checked for variation.

No statutory feed from the RBD database to pension bodies (EPFO, central/state pension disbursers), income tax, or health insurance (PM-JAY) was found; whether s. 3(5) notifications naming further databases have been issued was not checked.
Burial/cremation permits are governed by municipal law and State rules, not the Act; not researched.
No official death-verification service for banks/insurers found.
